dcf._tgWhy: Below the house 5-6% range on purpose: Indian coal demand is expected to keep rising into the 2030s (1 bn t target by FY30) but to plateau as renewables grow; 4% nominal (~flat volume plus inflation in prices) after year 15.

dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin drifts to 23% (FY26 24.5%): wage and diesel inflation, older underground subsidiaries, partly offset by e-auction and productivity.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~10% of revenue in FY27-29E falls to ~7% as evacuation and first-mile projects finish (by FY29-30, CARE); D&A ~6% of revenue.

cover.headline: A cash machine priced about right: ~6.5% yield, little growth, no pricing power
cover.lead: Coal India mines ~75% of India's coal and sells most of it to power plants at prices the Government effectively sets. After the FY23-24 e-auction windfall, EBITDA fell from ₹47,971 cr (FY24) to ₹41,243 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 EBITDA fell another 4% on diesel and contractor costs, but offtake rose 6.7% in Apr-Aug as power plants ran down their stocks. We forecast EPS of ₹{{F.eps.0|n1}} / ₹{{F.eps.1|n1}} / ₹{{F.eps.2|n1}} for FY27-29E. The street values Coal India on **EV/EBITDA on FY28E** (4.5-6x). Our multiple is derived, not picked: the stock's own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (4.0x), moved by the oil, gas and consumable-fuel peers' −6% against their five-year medians, gives **4x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹47,461 cr plus ₹75,821 cr of net cash = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: P/E ₹329, DCF ₹571. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The dividend is real and well covered
arguments.p: Coal India paid ₹26.50 a share for FY26 (52.5% of EPS) and declared ₹5.50 as the first FY27 interim. At our 52% payout the FY27E dividend is ~₹{{F.dps.0|n1}} (6.4% at ₹425), paid from ₹56,762 cr of cash and current investments (~₹92 a share) and free cash flow of ~₹{{F.fcf.0|num}} cr. The Government owns 61% and needs the cash, which keeps the payout high.

arguments.h: Volume is back, but growth is capped
arguments.p: Offtake fell 2.4% in FY26 to 745 MT; Apr-Aug 2026 offtake rose 6.7% to 322.9 MT while production fell 4.5% as pithead stocks were drawn down from 130 MT. Power demand grows, but captive and commercial mines (+10% to 210 MT in FY26) and renewables (coal's share of generation ~68% in FY26, from ~71%) take much of the increment. We assume +4.5% in FY27 and +3.5% a year after, against a 815 MT production target and a 1 bn t FY30 plan.

arguments.h: Prices: e-auctions swing, FSA does not
arguments.p: Over 85% of volume goes at notified FSA prices (₹1,444/t ex charges in FY26, ₹1,435 in Q1FY27) that did not rise from Apr-2025 to 30-Sep-2026 while diesel, explosives and outsourcing costs did. E-auctions (11-13% of volume) are the swing factor: premiums of 228% (FY23) and 99% (FY24) fell to 57% (FY26) and ~43% in Apr-Jul 2026. Low power-plant stocks (~8 days in September) could lift them again; the NCWA-XII wage settlement due from Jul-2026 is the cost on the other side.

arguments.h: Valuation: cheap on paper, fair on its own history
arguments.p: At ₹425 Coal India trades at 4.6x FY28E EV/EBITDA (net cash at Mar-26) and 7.9x FY28E EPS: cheap against the market, but in line with what investors have paid for it since 2021 (median 4.0x forward, 2-6x range). The street's 5-6x needs either a re-rating or EBITDA ~10% above ours (ICICI Direct's FY28E is ₹52,442 cr vs our ₹{{F.ebitda.1|num}} cr). We see fair value, a high yield and two-sided risk.

sections.title: What Coal India does: digs ~770 MT of coal a year and sells 80% of it to power plants

blocks.p: Coal India (CIL) is a holding company whose seven coal-mining subsidiaries produced 768 MT in FY26, about three-quarters of India's coal. Almost all of it (97%) comes from open-cast mines, where overburden (rock and soil) is stripped by contractors and the company's own machines; underground mines (25.6 MT) are small and old. It sold 745 MT: ~646 MT under fuel supply agreements (FSAs) at notified prices, mostly to power utilities with ~618 MTPA of linkages; ~84 MT through e-auctions, where buyers bid a premium over the notified price; and ~14 MT of washed coal and other products. About 79% of offtake goes to the power sector. Customers pay in advance for e-auction coal and largely for FSA coal, so receivables are only ~28 days. Revenue also carries ~₹650 a tonne of pass-through charges (royalty-linked levies, cesses, transport and evacuation recoveries).

blocks.p: Profit is concentrated: MCL (Odisha) and NCL (Singrauli, supplying pithead power stations) earned ₹21,355 cr of the subsidiaries' FY26 PAT; SECL ₹4,755 cr on more volume. ECL and BCCL, with older, deeper and partly underground mines in West Bengal and Jharkhand, barely break even or lose money (ECL −₹966 cr in FY26; BCCL −₹68 cr in Q1FY27). The group also owns stakes in fertiliser plants (HURL 30%, Talcher Fertilisers ~40%), coal gasification JVs with BHEL and GAIL (51%), solar plants (100 MW commissioned at Bhadramali, 200 MW of 300 MW at Khavda in Jul-2026) and rail-corridor companies.

blocks.callout: **The model in one line:** EBITDA ≈ tonnes sold × (FSA price for ~85% of volume + e-auction price for ~12%) − the cost of digging (wages ~₹46,400 cr, contractors ~₹32,200 cr, materials and power ~₹15,000 cr in FY26). With prices largely fixed, profit swings with volume, the e-auction premium and wage settlements.

sections.title: Industry: coal demand still grows with power, but Coal India gets a shrinking share of it

bullets: **Demand.** Coal is ~75% of India's power generation (CARE, Apr-2026); coal's share of generation fell from ~71% in FY25 to ~68% in FY26 while renewables rose from ~22% to ~26% (ICICI Direct, 30-Jul-2026). Thermal generation rose 9.9% in Apr-Aug 2026 and power-plant coal stocks fell to ~23 MT (~8 days) by early September (Equirus via Business Today, 10-Sep-2026).

**Supply.** Captive and commercial mines produced 210.5 MT in FY26 (+10%, vs 191.0 MT in FY25) and take a growing share of incremental output (CARE; ICICI Direct). Coal India produced 768 MT (-1.6%) and sold 745 MT (-2.4%) in FY26.

**Pricing.** FSA (notified) prices are set by Coal India with an eye on the Government and power tariffs; no general notified-price increase was announced between FY26 and 30-Sep-2026 (BCCL's WPI-linked coking-coal revision of +0.24% from Apr-2026). E-auction premiums over notified prices: 228% (PL basis, FY23), 99% (FY24), 69% (FY25), 57% (FY26); 36% in Q4FY26, ~47% in Q1FY27, 43% average Apr-Jul 2026 (Chairman, AGM).

**Policy.** GST on coal raised to 18% from 5% and the ₹400/t compensation cess abolished from 22-Sep-2025 (CARE). Supreme Court allowed states to tax mineral rights retrospectively (Coal India's estimate: ₹31,591 cr gross, ~₹6,000 cr net). Middle-East conflict raised diesel costs in 2026; Coal India chose to absorb them rather than raise prices (Kotak Neo, Apr-2026).

blocks.p: **Wages are the big unknown.** The non-executive wage pact NCWA-XI (19% minimum guaranteed benefit, 25% higher allowances) ran from Jul-2021 to 30-Jun-2026. We assume a ~10% rise on ~₹30,000 cr of non-executive pay from 1-Jul-2026, provided as it accrues: ~₹2,300 cr in FY27E and ~₹3,000 cr a year after, inside our EBITDA per tonne. blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** A scale-and-reserves franchise without pricing power: it earns a high ROE because the asset base is old and the State lets it, not because it can raise prices. Moat: narrow. The returns are real (ROE 28% in FY26) but they are a policy outcome: the Government sets prices low enough to protect power tariffs and high enough to fund its dividends.

sections.title: A windfall in FY23-24, a slow fade since: EBITDA ₹47,971 cr at the peak, ₹41,243 cr in FY26

blocks.p: Coal India's revenue was ₹77,861 cr in FY16 and ₹1,44,762 cr in FY24 on the old basis (net of statutory levies). From FY25 the accounts show levies that Coal India collects as principal (royalty-linked charges, cesses, transport and evacuation recoveries) inside revenue, after an auditor and C&AG observation: FY25 was restated to ₹1,69,177 cr and FY26 was ₹1,68,400 cr. About ₹48,300 cr of FY26 revenue (₹650 a tonne) is such pass-through charges, which also sit in costs, so the EBITDA margin on the new basis (24.5% in FY26) is not comparable with the 32-33% of FY23-24. EBITDA tells the real story: ₹18,628 cr in FY21, ₹44,232 cr in FY23 and ₹47,971 cr in FY24, when e-auction prices ran 228% and 99% above notified prices after the 2022 global coal spike, then ₹47,205 cr (FY25) and ₹41,243 cr (FY26) as premiums fell to 69% and 57% and volumes slipped. Net profit peaked at ₹37,402 cr (EPS ₹60.7) in FY24 and was ₹31,094 cr (EPS ₹50.5) in FY26.

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Coal India generated ₹1,78,988 cr of operating cash, spent ₹81,875 cr on fixed assets (Screener cash-flow basis; the company's own capex measure, which adds land, rehabilitation and JV equity, was ₹21,776 cr in FY25 and ₹19,607 cr in FY26) and paid ₹80,351 cr of dividends, about two-thirds of it to the Government. sections.title: Earnings quality: cash-backed, but restated revenue, capitalised stripping and one-off other income

bullets: **Revenue was restated.** From FY25, levies collected "in principal capacity" are inside revenue (auditor emphasis of matter; C&AG comment). Revenue and costs both rose ~₹29,000-32,000 cr; profit did not change. Screener's FY25 quarters remain on the old basis, so quarterly year-on-year revenue growth for FY26 is overstated.

**Overburden is partly capitalised.** When a mine strips more rock than its plan ratio, the excess cost becomes a "stripping activity asset" (₹4,071 cr credited to costs in FY26, ₹1,830 cr in Q1FY27) and is amortised later; the old ratio-variance provision is also being reversed into revenue (₹1,965 cr in FY26). Both lift EBITDA above the cash cost of the year. Screener moved the FY25-26 credit into other income; we put it back in costs (as in earlier years and all quarters) so EBITDA is comparable.

**Other income is flattered by items that fade.** FY26 other income of ₹11,276 cr included ₹2,365 cr of interest on income-tax refunds and ₹2,932 cr of provisions and liabilities written back: ~13% of pre-tax profit. We forecast ₹{{F.otherIncome.0|num}} cr in FY27E (incl. JV share) against ₹12,033 cr in FY26 and ₹12,555 cr in the year to Jun-26.

**Cash conversion is fine over time.** Cash from operations was 85% of net profit in FY25 and 139% in FY26 (₹43,215 cr; helped by lower taxes paid and working capital); it swings with customer advances and dues from power utilities.

**Big provisions and contingencies.** ₹77,763 cr of provisions (employee benefits, mine closure) at Mar-26; contingent liabilities ₹56,471 cr (Mar-25); the Supreme Court's mineral-tax ruling could cost ~₹31,591 cr gross, ~₹6,000 cr net of recovery from FSA customers (management via CARE). Not in our numbers.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Audited by statutory auditors appointed by the C&AG, unqualified, with emphasis of matter on the levies presentation and the stripping policy. Nothing improper, but reported EBITDA includes capitalised stripping and a provision reversal, other income includes ~₹5,300 cr of refunds and write-backs, and large contingencies sit off the balance sheet. We value on EBITDA as reported (the street does too) and forecast lower other income.

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹42,700 cr (₹69 a share), but large provisions for people and mine closure

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Coal India held ₹8,620 cr of cash, ₹43,955 cr of other bank balances (deposits, some earmarked) and ₹4,187 cr of current investments: ₹56,761 cr (~₹92 a share), against ₹14,072 cr of borrowings (mostly BCCL, ECL and rail-project loans, plus ₹251 cr of leases): net cash ~₹42,700 cr. It also holds ₹6,038 cr of JV equity (HURL, Talcher Fertilisers and others) and mine-closure escrow deposits that rose ₹2,251 cr in FY26. Against that sit ₹77,763 cr of provisions (employee benefits and mine closure), ₹19,815 cr of customer advances (e-auction and FSA buyers pay ahead) and contingent liabilities of ₹56,471 cr (Mar-25, CARE). GST on coal rose to 18% in Sep-2025, which lets Coal India use ~₹17,006 cr of accumulated input tax credit: ~₹8,000 cr in FY26 and the rest expected in FY27, extra cash our model does not count.

The Buys (MOSL ₹510, Anand Rathi ₹520, Jefferies ₹500) lean on the ~7% dividend yield, net cash and a stock at 4-5x FY28E EV/EBITDA; the Neutrals (Citi, JPMorgan ₹430, Morgan Stanley ₹420, ICICI Direct ₹480, Nuvama ₹454, Equirus ₹450, PL ₹472) see cheap valuation but no trigger; Kotak (Sell, ₹370) sees limited medium-term growth. Two upgrades in September (Nuvama, Equirus) were on e-auction premiums. The median target is ₹454, +7% vs the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹425. Every broker that discloses a method uses **EV/EBITDA on FY28E (or one year forward), at 4.5-6x**.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a ~6.5% yield at fair value; HOLD

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's dominant coal miner: ~75% of domestic output, ~49% of proven reserves, cheap open-cast mines, ~618 MTPA of power linkages and a balance sheet with ~₹42,700 cr of net cash (Mar-26). It pays out about half its profit, and its owner wants it to keep doing so.

**What you are paying:** 4.6x FY28E EV/EBITDA and 7.9x FY28E EPS, for EPS growth of ~2-4% a year with no pricing power on ~85% of volume. Since 2021 the market has paid a median 4.0x forward EV/EBITDA; oil, gas and consumable-fuel peers were 6.2% below their five-year median EV/EBITDA on 30-Sep-2026. On the street's method and the house multiple the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): HOLD. Add the ~{{F.divYield.0|n1}}% FY27E dividend yield and the expected 12-month return is ~8%, below our 12.5% cost of equity.

What it means
